_faq.title: Destinations & Itineraries FAQ
_faq.subtitle: Quick answers to plan routes between Morocco’s main regions.
_faq.q1: How many days do I need for a first trip to Morocco?
_faq.a1: 7–10 days works well for a classic loop (e.g. Marrakech + Sahara, or Fes + Chefchaouen). Two weeks lets you combine imperial cities, coast, and desert without rushing.
_faq.a2: Marrakech is livelier and the usual gateway to the High Atlas and Sahara. Fes is denser, more traditional, and pairs naturally with Chefchaouen and the north. Many travelers do both in 10+ days.
_faq.q3: How do I combine the desert with the cities?
_faq.a3: From Marrakech, allow 2–3 nights for Merzouga (Erg Chebbi) via the High Atlas and gorges. From Fes, the desert is farther; overnight stops in Midelt or Errachidia help. Private transfer or organized tour is easiest.
_faq.a4: Yes if you have at least 2 nights. It sits between Tangier/Tetouan and Fes. Ideal for a calm break between bigger cities, with day trips to Akchour waterfalls.
_faq.q5: Best region for a beach stop?
_faq.a5: Essaouira and Agadir on the Atlantic; Al Hoceima or Oued Laou on the Mediterranean. Essaouira pairs well with Marrakech (2.5–3h). Agadir suits longer beach stays and Taghazout nearby.
_faq.q6: Do I need a car to visit several destinations?
_faq.a6: Not always: CTM/Supratours buses and trains link major cities. A rental car (or private driver) is better for Atlas villages, desert gates, and flexible day trips.

faq.title: Destinations & Itineraries FAQ
faq.subtitle: Quick answers to plan routes between Morocco’s main regions.

q1.question: How many days do I need for a first trip to Morocco?
q1.answer: 7–10 days works well for a classic loop (e.g. Marrakech + Sahara, or Fes + Chefchaouen). Two weeks lets you combine imperial cities, coast, and desert without rushing.

q2.question: Marrakech or Fes first?
q2.answer: Marrakech is livelier and the usual gateway to the High Atlas and Sahara. Fes is denser, more traditional, and pairs naturally with Chefchaouen and the north. Many travelers do both in 10+ days.

q3.question: How do I combine the desert with the cities?
q3.answer: From Marrakech, allow 2–3 nights for Merzouga (Erg Chebbi) via the High Atlas and gorges. From Fes, the desert is farther; overnight stops in Midelt or Errachidia help. Private transfer or organized tour is easiest.

q4.question: Is Chefchaouen worth a detour?
q4.answer: Yes if you have at least 2 nights. It sits between Tangier/Tetouan and Fes. Ideal for a calm break between bigger cities, with day trips to Akchour waterfalls.

q5.question: Best region for a beach stop?
q5.answer: Essaouira and Agadir on the Atlantic; Al Hoceima or Oued Laou on the Mediterranean. Essaouira pairs well with Marrakech (2.5–3h). Agadir suits longer beach stays and Taghazout nearby.

q6.question: Do I need a car to visit several destinations?
q6.answer: Not always: CTM/Supratours buses and trains link major cities. A rental car (or private driver) is better for Atlas villages, desert gates, and flexible day trips.
